name: OW Agenda
author: OptionWeb

sections.description:
OW Agenda is a booking engine you configure, not code: a practice, a hair salon, a training centre, a workshop or a video consultation service all run on the same plugin.

  • Appointment types — each type has its own duration, opening hours (ranges or fixed start times), buffers, minimum notice, booking horizon, cancellation notice, capacity, daily cap, validation mode and announced response time.
  • Appointment modes — in person (address, directions, map link), phone (who calls whom, call instructions, phone number required), video (link) or other. Emails and calendar files adapt to the mode.
  • One shared calendar — no double booking, even between different types, and every manual appointment or blocked slot counts.
  • People and resources — practitioners, rooms or stations, each with their own agenda and, if needed, their own working hours. Two clients can book the same time with two different people; the visitor can choose with whom, or let the least busy one be assigned.
  • Group sessions — several places per time slot (workshop, class), and several places per booking (a family, a team).
  • Closure calendar — a month view to close a day, a week of holidays or a longer period for the whole agenda, one type, or the absence of one practitioner; also on the mobile agenda. Entered by hand, no external service.
  • Booking form per type — phone required, optional or hidden, message, and additional fields (short or long text, choice list, single or multiple choice, checkbox, number, date, email, phone, consent, photos), with conditional display, validated on the server.
  • Required photos — a type can ask for a number of photos (for example 2 to 4) before a booking is possible; without them, the booking is always refused. Photos are reduced in the browser, re-saved without their metadata, stored privately (never in the media library, no public address), attached to your notification email if you wish, and deleted automatically after the period you set.
  • Online changes — the customer moves their appointment to another free time slot from their email, within the notice you choose; with manual approval, you accept the new time like a new request.
  • Direct links and block — ?type=slug opens one booking path directly (ideal for an ad), [ow_agenda type="slug"] or [ow_agenda types="a,b"] restrict a page to some types, and the “Appointment booking” block does the same in the block editor.
  • Email double opt-in — a request only becomes real after the visitor clicks a validation link: bots and pranksters never reach the agenda.
  • Validation by the owner — manual or automatic per type; Confirm / Decline buttons right inside the notification email (signed links, no login required).
  • Editable emails — subject, heading, text and note per type and per email, with placeholders, preview and test emails sent only to you.
  • Mobile-first agenda — a login-protected “Agenda” page: day view with type colours and filters, pending requests, phone appointments added manually, blocked slots, rescheduling, customer directory, session invitations.
  • Import / export — the whole configuration in one JSON file, with a dry run before any change; WP-CLI commands and documented hooks for automation.
  • GDPR — explicit consent, WordPress personal data exporter and eraser, automatic anonymization of past appointments, no external service and no tracking.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the ow-agenda folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP via Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. The “Book an appointment” and “Agenda” pages are created automatically.
  4. Configure your appointment types, opening hours and emails in the OW Agenda menu, or import a configuration file in OW Agenda → Import / export.
sections.faq:
Do online slots take phone appointments into account?

Yes: every event in the agenda (web booking of any type, manual appointment, blocked slot) makes its time range unavailable for online booking.

Can I offer several kinds of appointments?

Yes. Add appointment types in OW Agenda → Appointment types. Visitors choose the type first; with a single type, the booking page looks exactly as before.

How do I send visitors straight to one type of appointment?

Add ?type= followed by the type slug to the booking page address, for example /book-an-appointment/?type=phone-call. The direct link of each type is shown in the list of types.

How do I close for the holidays?

In OW Agenda → Closures (or the “Closures” tab of the mobile agenda), select the days in the month calendar — one day, or a period by clicking its first and last day — then choose what closes: the whole agenda, one type, or the absence of one practitioner. Existing appointments are never cancelled: they are listed so that you can move them.

Several practitioners work at the same time. Can each one have their own agenda?

Yes. Create them in OW Agenda → Resources (with their own working hours if they differ), then tick them in each appointment type they provide. A time slot stays bookable as long as one of them is free. Tick “The visitor chooses with whom” to let visitors pick a practitioner or “No preference”.

Can customers move their appointment themselves?

Yes, if you allow it in the appointment type (“Online changes by the client”). The link in their emails then offers to change the date or time, within the cancellation notice and up to the number of changes you set. With manual approval, the moved appointment goes back to “pending” until you accept the new time.

Is OW Agenda available in French?

Yes. The French translation ships with the plugin for French (France) and French (Belgium) sites: nothing to install. If a WordPress.org language pack exists for your language, it is used first.

Can I require photos before a booking?

Yes. In the appointment type, add a “Photos” field to the booking form and set the minimum and maximum number of photos (for example 2 and 4). Visitors take or choose the photos from their phone; a booking without enough photos is refused, whatever the way it is sent. You see the photos in the agenda and, if you tick the option, attached to the new request email. They are deleted when the appointment is cancelled or declined, and automatically 30 days after the appointment (Settings).

Is there a block for the block editor?

Yes: “Appointment booking”, in the Widgets category. Its settings let you offer all types, one type, or a selection — like the shortcode.

How do I manage the agenda from a phone?

Open the “Agenda” page on your phone, log in, then use “Add to Home Screen”: it then behaves like an app.

Can customers cancel by themselves?

Yes, through the link in their emails, up to the cancellation notice of the type (24 hours by default). Past that, the page invites them to call.

Can I restyle the booking widget?

Yes. The widget reads CSS custom properties (--owag-accent, --owag-radius, --owag-text…) that your theme can override on .owag-booking. The email layout and the standalone pages are templates your theme can override in your-theme/ow-agenda/.

Does an update from 1.3 change anything for my visitors?

Your settings become a default appointment type with exactly the same opening hours, durations and rules, and your appointments and invitations are kept: visitors are offered the same time slots. Two things look different: the date picker lists available days only, and a declined request receives a “declined” email instead of a cancellation email.
sections.changelog:
1.6.1

  • New: French translation shipped with the plugin, for French (France) and French (Belgium) sites: the booking widget, the agenda and the emails are in French right after installation.
  • A WordPress.org language pack, or a catalogue placed in wp-content/languages/plugins/, still takes precedence; the shipped translation only fills the strings it lacks (for example the strings added by a newer version).

1.6.0

  • New: “Photos” form field — the visitor must send between a minimum and a maximum number of photos (1 to 10) for the booking to be accepted; the server refuses any booking without them, including direct API calls.
  • New: photos are reduced to 2,000 px in the browser, checked on the server (real JPEG, PNG or WebP image, size and dimensions), straightened, re-saved as JPEG without metadata (location, device) and stored in a private folder of the uploads directory, closed to direct access.
  • New: photos in the mobile agenda (thumbnails, full size on demand, for the people who manage the agenda only) and, as an option per type, attached to the new request email sent to the owner.
  • New: photo retention setting (30 days after the appointment by default); photos are also deleted when an appointment is cancelled or declined, when a request is never confirmed, on anonymization, on GDPR erasure and on uninstall, and a daily sweep removes any orphan file.
  • New: owag_is_uploaded_file filter and owag_photos_removed action.
  • Fixed: the appointment sheet of the mobile agenda no longer scrolls sideways (the notes field overflowed).

1.5.0

  • New: resources screen (practitioners, rooms, stations) with colour, description and optional own working hours. A time slot is offered for a resource only if it fits in its hours.
  • New: the visitor can choose with whom (or “No preference”); without a choice, the least busy resource of the day is assigned.
  • New: absence of a resource (holiday, training) as a closure — the other resources stay bookable.
  • New: month calendar of closures, in the administration and in the mobile agenda: select one day or a period, close the whole agenda, one type or one resource, edit or remove a closure in one click.
  • New: places per booking for group sessions; the booking form offers the number of places left.
  • New: form fields — single and multiple choice, number (with limits), date, email, phone, example text, and “show only if” conditions, all validated on the server.
  • New: online changes by the customer from their email, within the cancellation notice and a number of changes you set; emails “appointment moved” and “admin — moved by the customer”, calendar file updated.
  • New: “Appointment booking” block for the block editor.
  • New: {resource}, {seats} and {previous_datetime} email placeholders; owag_rescheduled and owag_resource_saved actions; REST routes for resources, month view and rescheduling.
  • Improved: the configuration import / export includes resources, their hours and their absences.

1.4.0

  • New: appointment types. Each type has its own duration, opening hours (ranges or fixed start times), buffers before and after, minimum notice, booking horizon, cancellation notice, capacity per time slot, daily cap, validation mode (manual or automatic) and announced response time.
  • New: appointment modes — in person (address, directions, map link), phone (who calls, call instructions, required phone number) and video (link). Emails and the ICS file (LOCATION, DESCRIPTION, URL) follow the mode.
  • New: exceptional closures (all types or one type, one day or a period) and exceptional openings for a type, entered by hand.
  • New: booking form per type — phone required, optional or hidden, message, additional fields (text, choice list, checkbox, consent) validated on the server.
  • New: type selector on the booking page, ?type=slug direct links, [ow_agenda type="…"] and [ow_agenda types="…"] attributes, CSS custom properties for theming, improved keyboard and screen-reader support.
  • New: editable emails per type and per status (received, confirmed, declined, cancelled, reminder, admin), placeholders, preview, and test emails sent only to the logged-in administrator. A declined request now gets a “declined” email instead of a cancellation.
  • New: JSON import / export of the whole configuration with a dry run, WP-CLI commands (wp owag), documented hooks, theme-overridable templates, WordPress personal data exporter and eraser.
  • New: resources (practitioners) at the engine level — a type can rely on several resources booked in parallel, with no overlap per resource.
  • Improved: the date picker lists the next available days only, with the next availability, instead of 14 calendar days with greyed-out days.
  • Fixed: the booking widget, the agenda and the settings screen failed on sites using “plain” permalinks.
  • Migration: on update, your settings become a default appointment type with identical behaviour; appointments, invitations and customers are kept. The migration runs once, automatically.

1.3.2

  • Confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.1.1 — no errors on activation, booking, agenda or settings.

1.3.1

  • Compliance: the standalone action, verification and cancellation pages no longer print their CSS and JavaScript inline. Both are now registered files served through the WordPress enqueue API, with the two variable button colours passed as CSS custom properties and the script configured through wp_localize_script().
  • Compliance: translation catalogues are no longer bundled. Only languages/ow-agenda.pot ships; French is delivered through the WordPress.org language packs fed by translate.wordpress.org.
  • Compatibility: the minimum WordPress version returns to 6.3, as nothing in the package depends on the bundled-translation discovery introduced in 6.7 any more.
  • REST: every administration route now declares its permission_callback explicitly instead of sharing it through array_merge(). The capability check was already enforced; it is now visible to static analysis as well.

1.3.0

  • Internationalization: the whole plugin is now translatable. Every user-facing string — admin settings, standalone booking and cancellation pages, REST messages, all e-mail templates and the JavaScript interface — uses the ow-agenda text domain with English as the source language. Domain Path: /languages is declared and languages/ow-agenda.pot ships for translators.
  • Localization: a full French translation has been produced from the original interface wording and submitted to translate.wordpress.org, so French sites get it through the standard WordPress language packs.
  • Security: appointment uid and invitation tokens are now generated with random_bytes() instead of wp_generate_uuid4(). These tokens are the sole authentication for public cancellation, e-mail verification and invitation booking, and the previous generator relied on a non-cryptographic PRNG.
  • Security: the public booking endpoint no longer accepts a missing honeypot or a missing timestamp — both silently disabled the anti-spam checks. The hourly quota is now aggregated per IPv6 /64 instead of per address, and a per-day cap limits unverified requests so a single visitor can no longer hold every slot of a day.
  • Security: the rate limit is applied after form validation, so a visitor who mistypes their e-mail is no longer locked out for an hour without any appointment being created.
  • Fixed: concurrent bookings of the same slot are now serialised with a named MySQL lock. The previous transaction issued a plain SELECT, which takes no row lock under REPEATABLE READ, so two simultaneous visitors could both book the same time.
  • Fixed: the day-before reminder used a fixed evening window and could be lost for good when no visitor triggered WP-Cron that evening. It now uses a sliding window (12 to 36 hours before the appointment) and catches up on the next cron run. Each reminder is claimed atomically before sending, so overlapping cron runs can no longer send it twice.
  • Fixed: the hourly cron event is re-scheduled automatically if it disappears, so reminders, purge and GDPR anonymisation cannot stop silently.
  • Fixed: rescheduling a confirmed appointment now updates the customer’s calendar. The ICS attachment carries a SEQUENCE, METHOD:REQUEST, organiser and attendee, and cancellations send a METHOD:CANCEL file that removes the event.
  • Fixed: the booking widget built its dates in UTC, so visitors east of UTC opening the page shortly after midnight saw the list start on the previous day and lost a day of availability.
  • Fixed: cancelling an appointment created from a private invitation now releases that invitation, which becomes usable and visible again instead of staying permanently dead.
  • Fixed: cancelled appointments and expired unverified requests are no longer returned to the agenda view, removing needless personal data from the REST response and phantom appointments from the admin calendar.
  • Removed: a leftover style rule from a client project that hid a third-party floating button on every page of the site.

1.2.1

  • Plugin Check compliance: output escaping, input sanitization, settings nonce, wp_delete_file(), readme.
  • Uninstall: also removes the customers table and the HMAC secret.

1.2.0

  • HTML emails (clean card layout, site accent color) for every notification.
  • Confirm / Refuse buttons in the admin email (HMAC-signed links).
  • Customer directory: search, create, edit, delete, shortcuts to new appointment and invitation.
  • Footer layout fix on the agenda page.

1.1.0

  • Email double opt-in against bots (slot held 45 minutes, purge after 48 hours).

1.0.0

  • Initial release: online booking, mobile-first admin agenda, session invitations, ICS emails and day-before reminder.

upgrade_notice.1.6.1: French translation included for French (France) and French (Belgium) sites. A WordPress.org language pack still takes precedence. No other change.
upgrade_notice.1.6.0: New "Photos" form field: require 2 to 4 photos (or any number up to 10) before a booking is accepted. Photos are stored privately, without metadata, and deleted automatically. Nothing changes for your visitors until you add the field.
upgrade_notice.1.5.0: Practitioners and resources, a month calendar to close days or periods, group bookings, richer form fields, online changes by customers and a block. Nothing changes for your visitors until you use them.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0: Appointment types, phone and video modes, closures, per-type forms and emails, JSON import / export. Your settings become a default type with identical behaviour; nothing to do after the update.
upgrade_notice.1.3.2: Confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.1.1. No code changes.
upgrade_notice.1.3.1: Compliance release: inline CSS and JavaScript on the standalone pages are now enqueued, translation catalogues are delivered through WordPress.org language packs, and REST permission checks are declared explicitly. No behavioural changes.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0: Security and reliability release. Cryptographic tokens, effective anti-spam, no more double-booking, reminders that cannot be lost, and calendar updates that actually reach the customer. The interface is now fully translatable (French included).
